title: One Transcript, Whole Stack: The Full Measurement of the SPXI Rent Event, Including Three Corrections to the Eyeballed Scores
creator: Sharks, Lee
description: The first end-to-end computation of the archive's measurement stack on a single transcript: attribution atoms, weighted PER with the M/C/D decomposition, Transit Rent with its observability gate, the Audit-Performance Bifurcation Operator, and Directionality of Semantic Labor span classes, with a cross-surface control at the same semantic address. wiki_article:
**One Transcript, Whole Stack** is the first end-to-end computation of the archive's measurement instruments on a single transcript, with a cross-surface control at the same semantic address.

**Its substance is that the computation disagreed with the scores assigned by eye, in three places.** PER is **0.824**, not 0.750, because the atoms that survived are the low-weight ones — both weight-3 atoms in the minimal dimension were absent. The acknowledgment score recorded as *source-level only* was **false**: the institution IS named in the first pass, so the pattern is **PER-M 1.00 with PER-C 0.67** — the organisation named, the persons withheld — which is a sharper finding than blanket omission. And the layer's invocation of the framework's own metric is a **Β measurement of ≈0.82** against a published threshold of 0.5, not a confession.

One result is worth stating on its own: **DSL is only −0.10.** A single enclosing span drags an otherwise task-advancing composition barely below zero. **Rent does not require a bad answer. It requires a good one with a position taken inside it.**

Limits are stated rather than buried: the atom set is stipulated, Β was computed by hand, span segmentation is the author's, and one case calibrates nothing.
